business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Procurement of Culinary and Ceremonial Grade Matcha

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Swiss Civil Code, Swiss Code of Obligations, and statutory overlay of regulatory public law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland-People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Protection Agreement (entered into force 15 June 1998)
Switzerland-People's Republic of China Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital, as amended by subsequent protocols
Switzerland-China Free Trade Agreement (entered into force 1 July 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: SR 220 (Swiss Code of Obligations, Arts. 626, 628, 950, 953); SR 221.411 (Handelsregisterverordnung/HRegV); SR 955.0 (Bundesgesetz über die Bekämpfung der Geldwäscherei und der Terrorismusfinanzierung, GwG); SR 955.033 (Geldwäschereiverordnung-FINMA); SR 955.071 (Verordnung über die beruflichen Sorgfaltspflichten im Finanzbereich); SR 311.0 (Swiss Criminal Code, Arts. 305bis and 305ter).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified copy of the passport or national identity document of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notarial authority in the UBO's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill, bank statement, or municipal certificate) for each UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank, or municipal authority in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or commercial register extract for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies house or commercial register in shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for the local Swiss incorporation representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the grantor's country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based PEP, OFAC, UN, and Swiss domestic sanctions screening under GwG Art. 2 para. 2 let. e and Art. 9a, read with FINMA Circular 2020/2. All UBOs, directors, signatories, and actual trading counterparties must be screened against (i) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (ii) the Swiss SECO consolidated sanctions list and corresponding economic measures; (iii) UK/EU/OFAC financial sanctions as best-market practice; and (iv) PEP databases and adverse media. Any PEP/UBO identification triggers enhanced due diligence (identity documentation, source of wealth, source of funds, and senior management approval); the low-risk tier of a matcha powder wholesale undertaking does not dilute the statutory screening duties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Swiss Commercial Register central index ZEFIX (www.zefix.ch) and the competent cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be composed in Latin characters and, as a rule, in one of the Swiss national languages (German, French, Italian, or Romansh); English is accepted as a complementary designation if not misleading. Foreign-language names undergo a transliteration check into Latin script, and the business purpose must be stated in the local registry language in a non-deceptive manner corresponding to wholesale of organic matcha powder.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On a preliminary adverse decision (Vorbescheid), the applicant must file a written reconsideration request with the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office within 10 calendar days, explaining why the proposed name does not violate Swiss firm-law requirements (OR Arts. 944-954, HRegV). If the refusal is confirmed, an appeal must be lodged within 30 days with the cantonal commercial-register or administrative appeal body; the final federal administrative instance is the Federal Commercial Register Commission (EHRA/CFRC), and decisions may thereafter be challenged before the Swiss Federal Administrative Court. A name-reservation extension must be requested before expiry; Swiss registry practice permits an extension of up to 90 additional days where UBO verification or apostille collection is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or maildrop is not acceptable as the statutory registered seat of an Aktiengesellschaft. For low-risk organic matcha powder wholesale, a serviced or managed office providing a physical address in the registered canton, authorized Swiss service of process, and local administrative support is permissible; the registered seat must be real, accessible, and professionally administered.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated 2% annual probability during the first year for a non-banking, low-risk trading company. Unannounced physical inspections are normally triggered by anomalies such as confirmed PEP matches, disclosed EU/UN sanctions, whistle-blower reports, or indications of fictitious domicile, and are not routine for standard wholesale commodity traders.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cantonal name search and preliminary name reservation / clearance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal tariff schedule for commercial register services (Handelsregistergebührenverordnung); CHF 70-120 market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the incorporation deed, articles-of-association execution, and bank certificate verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff and prevailing CHF 800-1,400 market benchmark for standard AG formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register entry fee for Aktiengesellschaft (AG)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for AG entries under HRegV; CHF 600-1,000 depending on canton

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation notice in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed official gazette publication fee; CHF 50-80

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille authentication of UBO, director, corporate shareholder, and power-of-attorney documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority / designated government office in each country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official apostille certificate tariff for four documents (varies by issuing state; estimated CHF 200-250)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign-language notarial documents into German or French for commercial register production
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing certified translator tariff per page and attestation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered Swiss physical office address and local corporate administrative / registered-agent service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss licensed fiduciary or corporate-services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing annual market benchmark for serviced office and registered agent in low-risk corporate-commodity trade

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO verification, PEP screening and KYC file transcription into Swiss due-diligence format
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Professional fiduciary / compliance agent engaged for incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated market compliance-administration fee (no direct public statutory charge).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft) as amended by the 2023 Stock Corporation Reform; Federal Act on the Commercial Register (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Bureau cantonal du registre du commerce), coordinated by the Federal Commercial Registry Office (EHRA), Swiss Federal Department of Justice and Police
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certified articles of incorporation (Statuten / actes constitutifs) authenticated by a Swiss notary and filed on the official Commercial Register submission form (Begleitschreiben with Form A)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital CHF 100,000 (registered shares, CHF 1.00 par value each); at least CHF 30,000 must be fully paid up in cash and deposited into a blocked bank account (Sperrkonto) prior to notarization, evidenced by a capital payment confirmation per Art. 632 OR; in-kind contributions must be fully covered by an audit or founder's report and charged to the capital
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscription of One Hundred Thousand (100,000) shares of CHF 1.00 nominal value each, fully paid up and evidenced by the bank confirmation of receipt, is hereby approved and allocated to the subscribing shareholders. RESOLVED that the registered office located at [Street, City, Canton], Switzerland is adopted as the statutory seat of the Company with immediate effect. RESOLVED that [Name] is appointed as sole member of the Board of Directors with individual signature authority, and [Firm] is appointed as independent statutory auditor (Revisionsstelle). RESOLVED that the Board is authorized to execute all Commercial Register filings, open corporate bank accounts, and complete all ancillary governmental registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Clearance and Central Index Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex, ZEFIX) operated by the Federal Commercial Registry Office (EHRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a preliminary query on ZEFIX to confirm the proposed company name satisfies the principle of truthfulness and non-deception (Art. 950 OR), contains no conflicting prior registrations, and clearly evidences the legal form 'AG/Société Anonyme'. The name must incorporate an activity descriptor consistent with the wholesale of organic matcha powder. Submit an optional preliminary reservation to hold the name for 3 months.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (three alternatives)
Legal form and summary of business purpose
Canton of registered office and correspondence address
Founders' identification details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as misleading or conflicting, file a written objection with the cantonal Commercial Register Office within 10 days supplying the corrected name and evidence of distinguishing business activity; non-substantiation results in re-indexing with alternative names.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Blocked Account Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank or securities dealer maintaining the blocked capital account (Sperrkonto)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate account under the intended company name with the bank, deposit a minimum of CHF 30,000 of paid-up cash capital, and instruct the bank to issue the statutory capital payment confirmation (Bestätigung der Einzahlung / attestation de libération) on the account, which remains blocked until the Commercial Register entry is completed. Complete AML/KYC verification including source-of-funds documentation.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of incorporation setting capital and share classes
Passport or identity card of each founder and director
Beneficial ownership declaration (Art. 628a OR)
Bank KYC forms and source-of-funds evidence
Proof of physical or virtual office address in Switzerland
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank escalates AML due-diligence queries, provide enhanced documentation (bank references, audited financial statements of shareholders, transactional trail) and, if declined by one institution, transfer the mandate to a second licensed bank; any delay extends the SLA by up to 5 additional business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal notary public (Notariat / Étude de notaire) designated for the registered office canton
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders must appear before the Swiss notary to execute the public deed containing the articles of incorporation (Art. 629 OR). The deed must state the corporate purpose (cross-border wholesale and distribution of culinary and ceremonial grade organic matcha powder under ISIC 4631), registered office, share capital, authorized share structure, and first board. The notary verifies the capital payment confirmation and the founders' signatures, then authenticates the deed and signs the organ declaration forms.
required_dossiers: Duly executed draft articles of incorporation
Capital payment confirmation from the bank (Sperrkonto evidence)
Valid passports and residency evidence of all founders and directors
Share subscription list (Zeichnungsschein / liste de souscription)
Office lease or consent of the owner to use the registered address
Mandate letter of the chosen statutory auditor (Revisionsstelle)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Should the notary identify an omission (e.g., defective clauses on capital contributions or in-kind valuations), the founders must reconvene for a supplementary deed; the application is returned with the notary's written rectification notice, and re-notarization is completed within 2 business days after delivery.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Filing and Legal Personality Grant
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered office canton
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized public deed, the completed official registration form (Form A), the organ declarations with specimen signatures, the auditor's acceptance declaration, and the capital payment confirmation. The Registrar verifies compliance with Arts. 640-641 OR (disclosure duties) and Art. 15 HRegV, issues the entry number, and arranges publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt). Legal personality is formally acquired upon registration as of the entry date.
required_dossiers: Notarized articles of incorporation (original certified copy)
Official Commercial Register submission checklist and Form A
Board of Directors organ declaration with specimen signatures
Statutory auditor acceptance declaration (Form 2 of the auditing standard)
Capital payment confirmation and bank release instruction
Identity and power-of-attorney documents of authorized representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query (Zwischenverfügung) on the corporate purpose or registered office, the legal counsel files a written clarification or an amended instrument within 20 days; failure to cure results in rejection with right of appeal to the cantonal supervisory authority (while knowing the applicant may refile without penalty).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Statutory Notifications to Federal and Cantonal Agencies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Social Insurance Office (BSV) through cantonal compensation offices; Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA); State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the mandatory AHV/IV/EO wage control registration with the cantonal compensation office for social security, register for occupational accident insurance with Suva or a licensed private insurer, apply for VAT registration with the FTA once taxable turnover reaches CHF 100,000 (goods supplied in Switzerland) or voluntarily upon formation, and file the employer registration instrument. Provide the Commercial Register extract to each authority as proof of legal capacity.
required_dossiers: Official Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug)
Copy of the notarized articles of incorporation
List of directors with nationality and residence details
Board resolution appointing payroll and insurance arrangements
Bank account details for social security debits
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration triggers administrative warning and retroactive contribution assessments; remedy by immediate filing with an explanatory letter and, if penalties are imposed, appeal to the cantonal social security authority demonstrating that the delay arose from statutory registry processing times.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO/BLV) acting through the cantonal food control authorities (kantonale Lebensmittelkontrolle); customs-compliant import control under the Federal Foodstuffs Act (Lebensmittelgesetz, LMG)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Operator Registration under Art. 82 LMG and Art. 11 of the Foodstuffs and Utilities Ordinance (LIV) – notification-based, not a discretionary license; mandatory registration with the cantonal food control authority and listing in the official FBO register

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU), acting with the cantonal environmental protection authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category G (no EIA required) because the activity is confined to warehousing, repackaging-in-sealed-bags, and wholesale distribution of dry matcha powder with no industrial production or Annex 10 facility of the EIA Ordinance (UVP-Verordnung) triggered
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emission sources; storage operations must comply with the Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV) for absence of contaminated runoff, the Waste Ordinance (VVEA) for separated disposal of packaging materials, and the Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance (ChemRRV) for any cleaning agents; temperature-controlled warehouse maintained below 20°C with relative humidity below 60% to preserve product integrity and prevent dust emissions in handling zones

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the cantonal building insurance authority (Gebäudeversicherung) validating fire suppression and emergency exit paths for the storage premises; structural load inspection certificate from the cantonal building authority confirming live-load capacity of the storage racking; occupational health clearance from Suva as the accident insurance carrier for the warehouse operation, including first-aid and hazard assessment per Art. 6 of the Labor Law (ArG)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC); official portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch and https://www.zefix.ch for UID registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG): (1) Incorporate and register in the Swiss Commercial Register; (2) obtain the Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer (UID) automatically from the Swiss Federal Statistical Office / Federal Tax Administration; (3) if taxable turnover exceeds the VAT registration threshold or an elective registration is made, file Swiss VAT registration through the ESTV ePortal (Form 700 / VAT registration); (4) the VAT identifier (MWST-Nr / TVA-Nr) is issued by the ESTV in the format CHE-123.456.789 MWST. A foreign entity without a Swiss registered establishment must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative when applying for VAT registration and provide a signed power of attorney and proof of foreign registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Swiss-resident stock corporations are subject to mandatory entity-level taxation at federal, cantonal, and municipal levels on worldwide income, with relief for foreign permanent establishments and real estate under double tax treaties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland has no check-the-box or hybrid pass-through election system. An AG is always taxed as a corporation. Available VAT elections include formation of a VAT group for closely integrated Swiss entities, and small-business election to register voluntarily despite turnover below the statutory threshold. Tax rulings may be obtained from cantonal and federal tax authorities for advance certainty on transactional tax treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide gross taxable turnover for businesses established in Switzerland. Foreign suppliers performing taxable supplies in Switzerland are generally required to register for Swiss VAT without a turnover threshold if no reverse-charge exemption applies. Importation of goods into Switzerland is exclusively subject to import VAT irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, digital stamping, or API tax clearance regime exists in Switzerland. Electronic invoices are permitted provided they ensure authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and readability as required by Article 26 of the Swiss VAT Act. Practical electronic invoicing formats include ZUGFeRD, EDIFACT, XML, and Swiss QR-bill-enabled invoices; VAT returns are submitted to the ESTV through its ePortal with machine-readable interfaces.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods are zero-rated if the goods are physically exported from Switzerland to a foreign destination and documentary proof of export is furnished to the ESTV. For the cross-border distribution of organic matcha powder, the exporter must demonstrate the goods left Switzerland, the export order was issued by a foreign party, and the transport completed to the foreign destination. Certain services supplied to foreign recipients are zero-rated where the place of supply is outside Switzerland, provided the recipient is established abroad and the service is actually used abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (Zollanmeldung / AES declaration)
Commercial Invoice describing organic matcha powder with HS/ISIC classification
Bill of Lading / CMR / Air Waybill as transport evidence
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer payment proof
Certificate of Origin (where required by the importing country)
Organic product certificate for the matcha consignment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration may retroactively review export zero-rating claims, and the statutory limitation period allows reassessment for several years after the tax year. If the required export evidence is missing, false, or not produced on time, the zero-rated treatment is denied, the VAT becomes immediately payable, and default interest is charged from the date the tax was originally due. Wilful or negligent false claims may trigger administrative fines under the Swiss VAT Act, with monetary penalties up to a maximum of CHF 800,000 for severe tax evasion cases, plus criminal prosecution where warrants.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains a fully liberalised currency regime for both current and capital account transactions under the Foreign Exchange and Currency Act; profit remittances, dividend distributions, and capital repatriation by non-residents are unrestricted, subject only to standard corporate law solvency tests and withholding tax compliance (final withholding tax at source), with no requirement for central bank approval or quantitative limits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory obligation to surrender export proceeds to the SNB or any authorised institution; export receipts may be held freely in CHF or foreign currency, credited to resident or non-resident accounts, and disposed of without mandatory conversion or a prescribed holding period.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility for fully offshore digital EMI reliance: Switzerland recognises only FINMA-authorised fintech (banking-like) licensees for domestic payment services; an EU/UK EMI operating purely offshore cannot clear CHF payments natively or maintain a Swiss IBAN, and would require a Swiss banking partner or a licensed Swiss fintech subsidiary; legal constraints under the Financial Services Act (FinSA) and Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) effectively mandate a regulated Swiss nexus for material treasury operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of the ultimate beneficial owner and at least one authorised signatory is generally mandatory for opening a corporate account with established Swiss tier-1 banks; although certain cantonal banks and fintech platforms permit fully remote video-identification under FINMA-approved procedures, the practical onboarding outcome for a CH-AG with cross-border matcha trade is a hybrid protocol—remote pre-screening followed by an in-person interview at the bank's registered Swiss office or at a Swiss embassy/consulate for overseas directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Specific Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) opacity, indirect ownership through foreign trust or foundation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of constitutive documents, full UBO chain chart with percentage holdings, sworn declarations of beneficial ownership, audited financial statements, and publicly verifiable register extracts (Swiss Commercial Register and foreign equivalent) presented to compliance officer for enhanced due diligence sign-off.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction transactions involving matcha sourcing from non-OECD Asia-Pacific producers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Verified supplier contracts, certificate of origin, phytosanitary and organic certification (Bio Suisse / EU Organic), Bills of Lading, pre-shipment inspection reports, and a clear transaction flowchart mapping counterparty banks to demonstrate no sanctions nexus or shell-company risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent third-party disbursements to brokers, agricultural cooperatives, or processing agents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial agency agreements, procurement due diligence pack, peer-reviewed independent audit of beneficiary status, risk-based transaction monitoring logs, and signed indemnity undertakings against misuse of accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of round-tripping or rapid in-out cash flows without corresponding trade documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Back-to-back purchase order evidence, customs declarations, encrypted freight forwarder data, and a complete audit trail from inbound SWIFT messages to outbound supplier payments stored in an immutable document repository made available to the bank's AML department.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/embargoes on end-user certificates for culinary vs ceremonial matcha grades
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-user declaration, certified commodity classification under HS 0902.10, no-re-export clause, and U.S. / EU / Swiss consolidated sanctions screening results for all parties to the transaction, refreshed with every new shipment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injection from overseas shareholder routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 with Swiss purpose code 'A130' (direct investment capital) or 'Y130' for repatriation back to investor; remitter bank must include the subscribing shareholder's KYC reference and Swiss company's commercial register number to accelerate final inbound verification; CHF or USD clearing settles through SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) for domestic leg, while cross-border leg adheres to the corresponding central bank RTGS procedure, with a confirmation obligation under the Federal Act on Monetary and the Payment Systems.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for supplier settlement of up to USD 250,000 per transaction; larger trade disbursements utilise documentary letters of credit (L/C) issued by the Swiss bank and advised through the beneficiary's bank, or standby L/Cs for confirmed purchase orders; all outbound payments in CHF settle through SIC; foreign-currency payments settle via correspondent banks in USD, EUR, or JPY with SWIFT STP (Straight-Through Processing) mandates to avoid manual intervention; MT700/MT710/MT720 trail ensures compliance with SWIFT UCP600 standards.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward forex contracts (Swiss banks and correspondent banks, tenor up to 12 months) marginally collateralised under Swiss Master Agreements
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) in restricted Asian currencies (JPY/CNY/INR) for underlying cross-border matcha procurement settlements
Currency swaps (FX swap / cross-currency interest rate swap) to manage USD/CHF and EUR/CHF liquidity gaps
Plain-vanilla European-style FX options (ITM/ATM/OTM) for asymmetric risk protection
FX forward rollovers and window forwards aligned with shipment milestones

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) resolution approving annual financial statements and discharging the board of directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting; minutes retained in corporate minute book (no filing with public registry required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the balance sheet date (typically no later than 30 June for 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil liability of directors for non-compliance; court may order convening at the expense of the company; administrative fines up to CHF 10,000 under Art. 731 and Art. 741a of the Swiss Code of Obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss federal and cantonal corporate income tax return including balance sheet and profit and loss statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax authority (e.g., Zug/Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) and Swiss Federal Tax Administration for direct federal tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing due within 6 months of the end of the business year, as stated in the cantonal tax request (extensions generally available upon application)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, default interest, compulsory assessment at the tax authority's discretion; continued non-compliance may lead to penalty surcharge of up to 30% of assessed tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / FTA), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 15 April for the prior calendar year if the company is filed on an annual basis; quarterly or semi-annual providers follow the intervening statutory deadlines of 15 April, 15 July, 15 October, and 15 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest at 4% per annum on late tax; surcharge up to 3% plus compounding for repeated violations; severe cases subject to criminal tax penalty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial register (Handelsregister) update filings and deeds of amendment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Mandatory registration within 3 months after a change in directors, authorized signatories, share capital, legal address, statutes, dissolution, or other registrable matters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to CHF 10,000 for failure to register; deregistration and administrative dissolution if commercial register determines the registered office is invalid or the company is inoperative

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit is mandatory if the AG exceeds two of the following in two consecutive fiscal years: balance sheet total above CHF 20 million, turnover above CHF 40 million, or average of 250 full-time employees. Companies not exceeding these limits may perform a simplified audit, unless shareholder protection rights require an ordinary audit; a simplified audit can be waived by unanimous shareholders' resolution only if the company has fewer than 10 full-time employees on annual average and fewer than 20 shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss GAAP FER (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles – Fachempfehlung zur Rechnungslegung) is mandatory for Swiss statutory financial statements; IFRS is mandatory for listed parent companies and may be voluntarily applied; tax accounts must be based on the audited or unaudited annual financial statements

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Art. 697j of the Swiss Code of Obligations, the AG must maintain a register of beneficial owners (wirtschaftlich Berechtigte) in Switzerland, updated whenever a shareholding reaches or falls below 25%. No annual filing to a public registry exists; an internal annual confirmation must be conducted by the board, recording all share transfers and direct shareholder declarations, and the register must be retained for a minimum of 10 years after deletion of the listed person.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (Register der wirtschaftlich Berechtigten)
Minute Book of shareholder resolutions and board resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 – USD 2,500 per year for a licensed Swiss registered office service in a mid-tier municipality
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 12,000 per year for simplified audit; USD 8,000 – USD 25,000 for ordinary audit depending on transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% Federal Direct Tax (income tax; 7.83% on a pre-tax grossed-up basis) + cantonal/communal profit taxes ranging 11.8%-21.0%; representative combined ordinary rate for a Zug AG: 14.6%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays exist. Effective reductions: 100% participation relief on qualifying dividends/capital gains; Swiss IP Box (90% exemption of qualifying IP income); 150% R&D super-deduction in selected cantons; relief for intercompany pure finance companies; notional interest deduction available in several cantons.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 2 / Steuererklärung juristische Personen (Form Tax Return for Legal Entities) submitted via the Federal e-Filing portal 'eTax FTA' plus the relevant cantonal portal (e.g., Zug e-Steuer); electronic filing is mandatory for AGs with a turnover above CHF 10 million.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (accounting period aligned to the statutory 12-month commercial year; calendar-year default for AGs).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due 30 June of the year following the balance-sheet date for a 31 December year-end; automatic extension granted until 15 December upon a reasoned request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1 - Net profit according to statutory annual financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Starting point: net taxable income per audited financial statements (Swiss GAAP FER, OR), expressed in CHF.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the full Swiss-branch or Swiss-company result including intra-group trading margin on matcha; confirm the treatment of pricing adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 - Add-back of non-deductible expenses (Art. 57 DBG / Art. 62 StHG)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back income taxes, Swiss withholding tax, penalties, personal benefits, and gifts/contributions not deductible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All transfer pricing penalties and Swiss interest/default surcharges remain non-deductible and must be added back for non-resident owners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 - Deduction of participation relief (Art. 69-71 DBG)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying dividends and capital gains from a shareholding of at least 10% held for at least one year are fully exempt after a 5% deemed non-business expense adjustment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Relief remains available notwithstanding non-resident shareholding, provided the Swiss AG itself meets the participation threshold and substance conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible business losses limited to the 7-year carryforward window under Art. 211 DBG and cantonal harmonisation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses from foreign permanent establishments or transparent foreign entities are not deductible in the Swiss return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable earnings after statutory adjustments; subject to the flat 8.5% federal direct tax without progression.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retained earnings are not attributed to non-resident shareholders; Swiss tax applies exclusively at the AG level until distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B - Taxable capital and reserves (cantonal tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Paid-in share capital, disclosed legal reserves, and other open reserves; participation deductions and IP-Box carve-outs reduce the base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cantonal capital tax and a 0.001%-0.5% rate apply irrespective of the non-resident ownership percentage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 27 - Tax credits and DTA relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Swiss withholding tax credits and foreign source tax credits applied against the federal/cantonal tax due; treaty relief attached.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File Form 820 (refund) or Form 820-A (relief at source) together with the Tax Residence Certificate of the ultimate shareholder to avoid double taxation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: reminder fees of CHF 30-250; coercive administrative fines up to CHF 30,000; default interest of 4.0% p.a.; penalties for incomplete/misleading filing range from CHF 100 to 3x the evaded tax; criminal complaints are possible in aggravated cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss Federal Withholding Tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on gross dividends paid to shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must submit Form 820 (Refund) or Form 820-A (Relief at Source) to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA), attaching a valid Tax Residence Certificate (Form 850-A) issued by the shareholder's foreign tax authority, evidence of beneficial ownership, shareholding percentage (at least 10% for the reduced 5% rate in many DTAs), and holding period; processing averages 8-12 weeks; most Swiss DTAs reduce dividend WHT to 5% (substantial participation) or 15% (portfolio).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% Swiss withholding tax on outbound royalty payments (no statutory WHT). Interest: 0% Swiss WHT on arm's length debt interest; however, 10% WHT applies on mortgage-secured interest but is reduced or exempted under most double taxation agreements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss TP documentation is required when cross-border intercompany transactions exceed CHF 10 million per annum; a Master File/Local File obligation is triggered for MNE groups with consolidated turnover exceeding CHF 100 million; even below these thresholds, a simplified TP study is mandatory for intra-group management services.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) as in zero-tax jurisdictions; nonetheless, the FTA enforces substance requirements through (i) participation relief requiring a 10% participation held at least one year, (ii) intra-group management services taxed at a minimum margin of 8%-10% on costs under FTA Circular No. 4, and (iii) Country-by-Country Reporting for groups with consolidated income above CHF 900 million. Insufficient local substance triggers denial of treaty and participation benefits and reclassification of retained profits as hidden distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Criminal Fiscal Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting or misstating cross-border matcha sales, inflating intercompany purchase prices from related Japanese producers, maintaining dual booking records, or submitting false balance sheets to reduce Swiss taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Federal direct tax penalty of up to 3x the evaded tax and a criminal fine of up to CHF 30,000 (Art. 175 and 186 DBG); VAT evasion penalties of up to 5x the evaded amount and a maximum CHF 2,000,000 fine (Art. 103 VAT Act); imprisonment up to 2 years in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for damages under Art. 754 Code of Obligations; the FTA may pierce the corporate veil where capital is demonstrably inadequate; administrative travel bans and exit restrictions may be imposed on directors as enforcement measures; personal imprisonment possible for criminal evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Letterbox AG with no physical premises, no Board meetings in Switzerland, no Swiss employees or management functions, sourcing all commercial decisions abroad while claiming Swiss participation relief and treaty benefits on dividend flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of participation relief and treaty refunds; retroactive 35% Swiss withholding tax on hidden profit distributions; prohibition of favourable tax treatment for a period of up to 5 fiscal years; mandatory capital tax recapture; potential administrative liquidation of the registered office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for uncollected withholding tax and penalties (Art. 12 DBG); Swiss courts may declare the director personally responsible for restitution of treaty benefits wrongfully claimed; travel bans and seizure of personal assets in insolvency proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intra-group matcha powder transactions priced outside arm's length, reducing the Swiss margin below the benchmark net margin (e.g., an affiliate in a low-tax jurisdiction earning excess margin while the Zurich/Zug AG continually incurs losses or marginal profits); absence of contemporaneous TP documentation and CbC inconsistencies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward tax adjustment of taxable profit; penalty of up to 3x the under-declared tax; default interest of 4% p.a. on the additional assessment; application of the hidden dividend doctrine leading to 35% WHT exposure on transfer pricing adjustments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign non-compliant returns or implement artificial pricing structures face civil liability for restoration of corporate assets under Art. 678 OR, joint liability under Art. 754 OR, and criminal sanctions in case of fraudulent intent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Tolerating unattributed SWIFT wire transfers, accepting cash payments above CHF 15,000 without KYC verification, implementing invoice-splitting to circumvent AML thresholds, or routing matcha trade proceeds through shell intermediaries in non-compliant jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty for aggravated money laundering under Art. 305bis/305ter Swiss Criminal Code: imprisonment up to 5 years and a corporate fine up to CHF 5,000,000; confiscation of assets under Art. 70 SCC; fines under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG) up to CHF 500,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors implicated in laundering operations face imprisonment and mandatory exclusion from equivalent business for 10 years; personal monetary restitution is ordered pursuant to Art. 58a SCC; international arrest warrants and Swiss asset freezes are coordinated through mutual legal assistance channels.
